Position Summary Are you ready to help some of the world’s leading infrastructure organizations turn ambitious business outcomes into clear, achievable technical direction? Bentley is looking for a Technical Account Manager (TAM) to act as a strategic technical partner to our most important accounts. Working in tandem with the Account Manager, you will build a deep understanding of what our customers are trying to achieve, identify what is preventing them from getting there today, and bring together the right Bentley people, technology and expertise to shape the right way forward. This is not a role centered on simply presenting products. You will help customers make important technical decisions across complex organizations, workflows and technology landscapes. You will connect business ambition with technical strategy, make the complex easier to navigate, challenge assumptions when needed, and ensure the solutions we recommend genuinely address the customer’s needs. Sometimes that will mean helping a customer get more value from Bentley technology they already own. Sometimes it will mean introducing new capabilities. Where specialist expertise or Services are needed, you will bring them in at the right time. The objective is always the same: the right solution for the customer’s challenge, with a clear path to lasting value. The TAM role sits within Bentley’s Solution Engineering organization and is predominantly pre-sales. Success comes from creating positive customer impact, progressing technically sound opportunities, increasing effective product consumption and supporting sustainable recurring revenue growth because our customers are succeeding with Bentley. Responsibilities Partner with Account Management and Value Engineering to understand each customer’s business drivers, ambitions, desired outcomes and measures of success, and use these as the reference point for technical decisions. Lead and orchestrate technical discovery to establish the customer’s current environment, including workflows, technology, data, architecture, integrations, constraints and organizational capability. Identify the evidenced capability gaps that prevent the customer’s current environment from achieving the outcomes they are seeking. Shape the recommended future direction with the customer and the appropriate Bentley specialists, translating business needs into a clear To-Be state and agreed Technical Intent. Ensure Bentley solutions are positioned because they are the right fit for the customer’s challenge - not simply because more technology or more Services could be sold. Help customers understand the art of the possible through workshops, solution discussions, demonstrations, proofs and specialist engagement appropriate to the opportunity. Technically qualify and progress known opportunities, identify and remove material technical barriers, and drive opportunities towards Technical Closure. Discover new opportunities by identifying genuine customer needs that Bentley can help address through existing capabilities, new solutions, expanded usage or appropriate Services. Increase effective product consumption and support sustainable ARR growth by helping customers gain broader and deeper value from Bentley capabilities. Identify, assemble, brief and coordinate the right Solution Architects, Application Engineers, Subject Matter Experts, Product specialists and other contributors for both single-product and multi-product opportunities. Maintain one coherent technical story across specialist contributions so that products, architecture, workflows and Services remain aligned to the same customer outcomes. Own and maintain the Technical Strategy Plan as the single source of truth for the customer’s technical direction, linking business drivers to current state, capability gaps, future state, opportunities, initiatives and decisions. Give Services early visibility of credible opportunities where delivery expertise may be required; collaborate on scope development and ensure a clear, high-quality handover when execution transfers to Services. Support account planning and the Bentley Sales Process, and use Salesforce and agreed account tools to document the information required to progress opportunities and maintain account continuity. Stay informed about infrastructure industry trends, customer challenges, Bentley solutions, relevant standards and competitive technologies so that advice remains current and credible. Build trusted relationships with customer stakeholders at different levels, from technical practitioners to senior leaders, and communicate consistently, clearly and in a way that helps customers make confident decisions. Foster a culture of 'One Bentley' by collaborating across Sales, Solution Engineering, Value Engineering, Services, Support, Product and Technology in a way that benefits our accounts. This is an individual contributor, full-time role. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in engineering, technology, computer science, construction, infrastructure, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience. 10+ years’ relevant experience in infrastructure technology, engineering software, digital transformation, enterprise solutions, technical consulting, solution engineering or a comparable environment. Strong customer-facing experience, ideally in technical pre-sales, solution consulting, strategic technical account management or enterprise architecture. Demonstrable ability to understand business goals and translate them into practical technical direction, solution requirements and next steps. review_candidates.title: Sr Spec, LEARN Emerg Resp
review_candidates.description: JOB SUMMARY: The Senior Specialist, LEARN Emergency Response will oversee International Medical Corps' infectious disease response portfolio under the LEARN project and separate donor funding, and serve as the primary liaison between field-based response teams and donor representatives. Based in Washington, D.C., the position will provide coordination, communication, and operational support to ensure effective implementation of outbreak response activities while maintaining strong donor engagement and compliance. Working closely with country offices, regional platforms, technical advisors, grants management, monitoring and evaluation teams, and senior leadership, the Senior Specialist will ensure timely information flow, effective decision-making, donor reporting, and alignment of infectious disease response activities within broader LEARN project objectives and International Medical Corps' organizational priorities. This position plays a critical role in supporting emergency surge operations, monitoring outbreak developments, identifying operational bottlenecks, facilitating cross-functional coordination, and ensuring donor requirements are met through high-quality reporting and communication. To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation. Main Tasks And Responsibilities Program Coordination and Response Management Serve as the primary focal point for International Medical Corps' infectious disease response activities under the LEARN project. Coordinate communication and information sharing between field response teams, regional platforms, headquarters departments, and organizational leadership. Monitor outbreak developments and response implementation across affected countries and provide timely analysis and recommendations to leadership. Track response priorities, action items, operational challenges, and critical decisions to ensure effective implementation. Facilitate coordination among technical, operational, security, logistics, finance, grants, and program quality teams supporting ID response activities. Support rapid response scale-up efforts and facilitate surge coordination during outbreak emergencies. Identify programmatic and operational risks and work with relevant stakeholders to develop mitigation measures. Foster a continuous understanding of the outbreak operating environment and emerging response needs. Donor Liaison and External Representation Coordinate donor communications, updates, briefings, presentations, and response-related meetings. Lead preparation for donor engagements by collecting inputs from field teams and cross-functional departments. Ensure donor communications accurately reflect operational realities, response achievements, challenges, risks, and funding needs. Prepare donor briefing materials, situation updates, presentations, and meeting summaries. Support donor visits, virtual briefings, and monitoring activities as required. Represent International Medical Corps in external meetings, coordination forums, and technical discussions as delegated by senior leadership. Reporting, Analysis, and Information Management Analyze and synthesize field data, operational updates, epidemiological information, and response metrics from country teams and regional platforms. Produce high-quality donor reports, situation reports, briefing papers, executive summaries, and response updates. Develop and maintain systems for tracking key response indicators, milestones, risks, and action items. Ensure accurate and timely information sharing with internal and external stakeholders. Support development of strategic analyses to inform leadership decision-making and response planning. Proposal Development and Resource Mobilization Support the development of emergency funding proposals, modifications, and cost extensions related to ID preparedness and response activities. Coordinate inputs from technical, operational, finance, and country teams for proposal development. Assist with donor negotiations and funding discussions as requested. Ensure proposed activities align with donor requirements, operational realities, and strategic response objectives. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning Collaborate with Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) teams to track response performance and outcomes. Ensure response data is incorporated into broader LEARN monitoring and reporting frameworks. Support learning reviews, after-action reviews, and documentation of best practices and lessons learned. Promote evidence-based decision-making through data analysis and performance monitoring. Cross-Departmental Coordination Collaborate with Grants, Finance, Compliance, Security, Human Resources, Logistics, Procurement, Communications, and Program Quality teams to support effective response implementation. Facilitate timely review and approval of agreements, budgets, reports, and operational requests related to ID response activities; act as ID response budget manager as assigned by Sr. Leadership. Ensure compliance with donor regulations, International Medical Corps policies, and organizational standards. Support organizational leadership in addressing complex operational, compliance, and risk management issues. Knowledge Management and Capacity Strengthening Develop tools, templates, guidance documents, and coordination mechanisms to strengthen outbreak response management. Support documentation and dissemination of lessons learned and best practices from response operations. Contribute to strengthening organizational emergency response systems and preparedness efforts. Security and Duty of Care Support implementation of organizational safety and security policies related to response activities. Coordinate with security personnel to monitor operational risks and ensure appropriate follow-up actions. Promote staff safety, well-being, and adherence to duty-of-care standards during emergency operations. Perform other duties as assigned. The duties and responsibilities listed in this document are representative of the nature and level of work assigned and not necessarily comprehensive. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s degree (master’s preferred) in Public Health, Epidemiology, Infectious Diseases, International Development, Humanitarian Assistance, Global Health, International Relations, or a related field. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be substituted as appropriate. Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian health programming and emergency response. Minimum 3 years of experience managing infectious disease outbreak responses, including Ebola, Marburg Virus Disease, cholera, or similar public health emergencies. Demonstrated experience coordinating complex, multi-country humanitarian response programs. Proven experience serving as a donor liaison and managing relationships with U.S. Government and institutional donors, including USAID/BHA, U.S. Department of State/PRM, CDC, ECHO, and other bilateral or multilateral donors. Strong experience in donor reporting, proposal development, cost modifications, and grants management. Experience supporting emergency response operations across multiple countries and regions. Strong understanding of outbreak preparedness, response coordination, health systems strengthening, and humanitarian health programming. Experience working with monitoring, evaluation, and learning systems in humanitarian settings. Demonstrated ability to analyze complex information and communicate effectively to diverse audiences. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including exceptional report writing and presentation abilities. Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Proven ability to work effectively across cultures, time zones, and multidisciplinary teams. Excellent problem-solving, strategic thinking, and decision-making skills. Ability to remain flexible and perform effectively in fast-paced and rapidly changing emergency environments. Full professional proficiency in English required; professional proficiency in French and/or Arabic strongly preferred. Commitment to the values, mission, and principles of International Medical Corps. Humanitarian health emergency response leadership. Ebola and infectious disease outbreak coordination. Donor engagement and strategic communication. Program management and operational oversight. Proposal development and grants management. Data analysis and strategic reporting. Cross-functional leadership and stakeholder engagement. SALARY RANGE: Mid $80's up to $105K per year For positions filled in the United States, the typical salary range for this role is as stated above. Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, job level, internal equity and budget. Exact salary offers will be determined by factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, experience and geographic location.

Four to six (4-6) years of experience in finance, commercial banking, renewable energy or other energy-related fields.
